common.tagline: Mini games for math and computer science

landing.title: Games for the classroom.
landing.subtitle: As an introduction, a break, or just in between.
landing.description: Pick a game, show the 6-digit code — the class plays along instantly. No account needed for students.
landing.step1: Choose a game and create a lobby

game.allAnswered: All questions answered! Waiting for others...
game.hostView: Players are answering. Watch their progress:
game.hostInfo: Explain the rules, then click 'Let's go!' to start.

lobby.title: Lobby
lobby.shareCode: Share this code with your class

example.title: Example Game
example.description: A one-stage example game to test the framework.

tap.name: Tap Race
tap.summary: Click as often as you can
tap.rules: Click as many times as possible in {{duration}} seconds. Target: {{targetScore}} clicks!

squareroot.title: Square Root Challenge
squareroot.description: Square roots as a speed round, on the number line and by category.
squareroot.clickOnLine: Click on the number line to estimate the value
squareroot.simplifyHint: Leave the factor empty for 1, and the radicand empty for a whole number. Pull every square out of the root.
squareroot.bisectPrompt: Is √{{value}} smaller or larger than {{mid}}? Pick the half it lies in.
squareroot.bisectDone: The interval is narrow enough ({{target}}). Submit it!

speed.name: Speed Round
speed.summary: Solve perfect square roots as fast as possible
speed.rules: Solve {{questionsPerRound}} square roots as fast as possible. All answers are natural numbers. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

numberline.name: Number Line
numberline.summary: Estimate irrational roots on the number line
numberline.rules: Estimate {{questionsPerRound}} square roots by clicking on the number line. The closer you are to the real value, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

classify.name: Classify
classify.rules: Classify {{questionsPerRound}} square roots as natural, rational or irrational. Each correct answer is worth 100 points. You have {{duration}} seconds.

simplify.name: Root Laws
simplify.summary: Write roots as simply as possible
simplify.rules: Simplify {{questionsPerRound}} root terms — no calculator. Pull every square out of the root: √72 becomes 6√2. You have {{duration}} seconds.

bisect.name: Interval Halving
bisect.summary: Trap an irrational root step by step
bisect.rules: Trap {{questionsPerRound}} roots between two numbers. Halve the interval again and again and always keep the root inside — the fewer halvings, the more points. You have {{duration}} seconds.

analysis.title: Analysis Challenge
analysis.description: Calculus: pick the derivative, draw the graph, draw the derivative.
analysis.pointsHint: Work out the y-intercept and the turning points first, then drag the {{count}} points there — the curve follows them.
analysis.pointsExtraHint_one: Tap the grid for one more point, tap a point to take it away again.
analysis.pointsExtraHint_other: Tap the grid for up to {{count}} more points, tap a point to take it away again.

multiple-choice.name: Pick the Derivative
multiple-choice.rules: Pick the correct derivative f'(x) from 4 options for {{questionsPerRound}} functions. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

draw-graph.name: Draw the Graph
draw-graph.summary: Sketch f(x) on the coordinate grid
draw-graph.rules: Draw the graph of {{questionsPerRound}} functions on the coordinate grid. The more accurate your drawing, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

draw-derivative.name: Draw the Derivative
draw-derivative.summary: Sketch f'(x) from the graph of f(x)
draw-derivative.rules: Draw the derivative f'(x) for {{questionsPerRound}} given functions. The dashed curve shows f(x). You have {{duration}} seconds.

rational.title: Rational Numbers
rational.description: Place rational numbers on the number line and calculate with them.
rational.arrangePrompt: Pick a number, then click on the number line
rational.arrangePromptSelected: Click on the number line to place the selected number

answerHint.fraction: Leave the denominator empty for a whole number. Equivalent fractions count as correct.
answerHint.decimal: Enter the result as a decimal, e.g. 0.75.
answerHint.both: Enter the result as a fraction (3/4) or as a decimal (0.75).

rational.signPrompt: Is the result positive or negative?
rational.changeAskResult: Click on the number line where you end up.
rational.changeAskChange: Which change leads from the start to the end state?

arrange.name: Arrange on the Number Line
arrange.summary: Place fractions and decimals at the right spot
arrange.rules: Place {{questionsPerRound}} sets of rational numbers on the number line. The closer each number sits to its real position, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

calculate.name: Calculate
calculate.summary: Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions
calculate.rules: Solve {{questionsPerRound}} calculations with rational numbers and enter the result. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

signs.name: Sign Duel
signs.summary: Work out terms with positive and negative numbers
signs.rules: Solve {{questionsPerRound}} terms with positive and negative numbers — no calculator. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

change.name: Changes
change.summary: Follow a change on the number line
change.rules: Follow {{questionsPerRound}} changes: place the end state on the number line, or name the change that leads there. You have {{duration}} seconds.

chance.title: Chance
chance.description: Work out probabilities and fill in tree diagrams.

laplaceHint.fraction: Favourable outcomes over possible outcomes. Equivalent fractions count as correct.
laplaceHint.decimal: Enter the probability as a decimal, e.g. 0.25.
laplaceHint.percent: Enter the probability in percent, e.g. 25.

chance.treePrompt: Drag the probabilities onto the second-stage branches — or tap a card and then a branch.
chance.treeIncomplete: Every branch of the second stage needs a probability.

setups.cards: One card is drawn from a deck of 32 cards.
setups.urn: An urn holds {{red}} red and {{blue}} blue balls. You draw one ball.
setups.wheel: A wheel of fortune has {{sectors}} equal sectors, {{winning}} of them win.
setups.urnTwiceWith: An urn holds {{red}} red and {{blue}} blue balls. You draw one ball, put it back, and draw again.
setups.urnTwiceWithout: An urn holds {{red}} red and {{blue}} blue balls. You draw two balls without putting the first one back.
setups.wheelTwice: A wheel of fortune has {{sectors}} equal sectors, {{winning}} of them win. You spin it twice.

laplace.name: Laplace Sprint
laplace.rules: Work out {{questionsPerRound}} probabilities: favourable outcomes over possible outcomes. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

tree.name: Tree Diagram
tree.summary: Fill in a two-stage tree and use the path rules
tree.rules: Complete {{questionsPerRound}} tree diagrams: place the probabilities on the branches of the second stage, then work out the probability of the event. Multiply along a path, add the paths. You have {{duration}} seconds.

extremum.title: Extreme Values
extremum.description: Differentiate without a calculator and solve extreme value problems.
extremum.deriveUnreadable: That cannot be read as a polynomial yet.
extremum.modelPrompt: Which constraint and which target function belong to this situation?
extremum.modelIncomplete: Pick a constraint and a target function first.
extremum.optimizePrompt: Now move x until the quantity is as large as possible.

contexts.fence: A rectangular pasture lies along a straight river. {{length}} m of fence are available for the three sides that are not the river. How wide does it have to be to get the largest area?
contexts.box: An open box is folded from a square sheet with side {{side}} cm by cutting squares of side x out of the corners. Which x gives the largest volume?
contexts.parabola: A rectangle stands on the x-axis with its upper corners on the parabola y = {{height}} - x². Which x gives the largest area?

derive.name: Derivative Sprint
derive.rules: Differentiate {{questionsPerRound}} polynomials — no calculator, as in the written exam. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. You have {{duration}} seconds.

optimize.name: Extreme Value Problem
optimize.summary: From the constraint to the target function to the maximum
optimize.rules: Solve {{questionsPerRound}} extreme value problems: pick the constraint and the target function, then find the value of x that makes the quantity largest. Half the points come from the model, half from the maximum. You have {{duration}} seconds.

settings.stagesHint_one: One round per active stage (1 round).
settings.stagesHint_other: One round per active stage ({{count}} rounds).
settings.twoChanges: Sometimes two changes in a row
settings.showTargetGraph: Show the graph of the target function
